hook: Geoffrey Hinton spent decades arguing that computers could learn the way brains do, by tuning the connections between simple units, during years when most of the field had turned away from neural networks. His Boltzmann machines, his part in bringing backpropagation into wide use, and the 2012 image recognition network he built with his students Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever helped make deep learning the main method in AI. He shared the 2018 Turing Award with Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun and the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield. In 2023 he left Google so that he could speak openly about the risks of the technology he helped build.
name: Geoffrey Hinton

quote.text: The unique problem with AI is that if it goes wrong, if it takes over, you don't get a second chance.
quote.context: Interview with The Guardian, 13 October 2026, explaining why uncertainty about AI's future is no reason for complacency

timeline.event: Graduates from Cambridge with a BA (Hons) in experimental psychology
timeline.impact: Starts out studying the mind, the source of the brain-inspired view of computing he later pursued

timeline.event: Awarded a PhD in artificial intelligence by the University of Edinburgh for research carried out from 1972 to 1975
timeline.impact: Trains in AI under Christopher Longuet-Higgins, who favoured the symbolic approach that Hinton went on to challenge

timeline.event: Joins Carnegie Mellon University as an assistant professor, later associate professor, after research posts at Sussex, UC San Diego and the MRC Applied Psychology Unit in Cambridge
timeline.impact: Gives him a US base during the years his best known early papers appeared

timeline.event: Publishes A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines with David Ackley and Terry Sejnowski in Cognitive Science
timeline.impact: Introduces a network that finds hidden structure in data using methods from statistical physics, the work the Nobel committee later highlighted

timeline.event: Co-authors Learning representations by back-propagating errors with David Rumelhart and Ronald Williams in Nature
timeline.impact: Shows that backpropagation lets layered networks learn their own internal representations and helps make it the standard training method, though earlier versions of the technique existed

timeline.event: Becomes a professor of computer science at the University of Toronto and a fellow of the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research
timeline.impact: Toronto becomes his base for the rest of his career, apart from three years in London

timeline.event: Moves to University College London as founding director of the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, and is elected a Fellow of the Royal Society
timeline.impact: Leads a new centre for computational neuroscience before returning to Toronto in 2001

timeline.event: Presents ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, written with Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever, at NIPS
timeline.impact: Their network, later known as AlexNet, cuts image recognition error far below earlier methods and turns computer vision toward deep learning

timeline.event: Google acquires DNNresearch, the company he formed with Krizhevsky and Sutskever, and he starts working half time at Google
timeline.impact: His group's methods move into one of the largest technology companies, while he keeps his University of Toronto post

timeline.event: Becomes Chief Scientific Adviser to the Vector Institute in Toronto
timeline.impact: Gives his backing to a new Toronto centre for AI research in an unpaid role

timeline.event: ACM names him, Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun recipients of the 2018 Turing Award
timeline.impact: Computing's top prize, worth $1 million, honours the three for making deep neural networks central to computing

timeline.event: Leaves Google in May after about ten years so that he can speak freely about the dangers of AI
timeline.impact: Becomes one of the most prominent voices warning about misinformation, job losses and the risk of AI escaping human control

timeline.event: Shares the Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield
timeline.impact: The prize recognises foundational discoveries behind machine learning with artificial neural networks, with Hinton's share tied to the Boltzmann machine

timeline.event: Receives an honorary doctorate from Harvard at its May Commencement
timeline.impact: One of five honorary degrees Harvard conferred that year, with the Crimson pointing to his foundational work in AI

quick_facts: Born on 6 December 1947 in London, he holds Canadian citizenship as well as British
Holds a BA (Hons) in experimental psychology from Cambridge (1970) and a PhD in artificial intelligence from Edinburgh, awarded in 1978
University Professor Emeritus in the Department of Computer Science at the University of Toronto, his base since 1987 apart from three years in London
Chief Scientific Adviser to the Vector Institute since 2017, an unpaid role
Worked half time at Google from March 2013, after it bought his startup DNNresearch, and left in 2023 as a VP and Engineering Fellow
Shared the 2018 ACM Turing Award with Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun, and the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield
One of seven engineers awarded the 2025 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering for modern machine learning

achievements.title: Boltzmann machines (1985, with David Ackley and Terry Sejnowski)
achievements.impact: One of the first neural networks that could learn internal representations in hidden units, built with ideas taken from statistical physics. The Nobel Foundation's account of his 2024 prize centres on this work.

achievements.title: Backpropagation paper in Nature (1986, with David Rumelhart and Ronald Williams)
achievements.impact: Showed by experiment that layered networks trained with backpropagation discover useful internal representations, and helped make the method the standard way to train neural networks. Credit for the method is disputed. Hinton said in a 2018 interview that Rumelhart came up with the basic idea, and Jürgen Schmidhuber argues that earlier work by Seppo Linnainmaa, Paul Werbos and Shun'ichi Amari, among others, has gone under credited by Hinton and by the Nobel award.

achievements.title: AlexNet (2012, with Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever)
achievements.impact: A deep convolutional network with about 60 million parameters, trained on GPUs with rectified linear units and dropout, that beat earlier image classifiers by a wide margin. ACM credits it with nearly halving the ImageNet error rate and reshaping computer vision.

achievements.title: DNNresearch and Google (2013)
achievements.impact: Google bought DNNresearch, the startup he formed with Krizhevsky and Sutskever, reportedly for $44 million. That brought his group's methods into Google, where he worked half time for a decade while keeping his Toronto post.

achievements.title: Turing Award and Nobel Prize
achievements.impact: The 2018 ACM Turing Award honoured him, Bengio and LeCun for the ideas and engineering that put deep neural networks at the centre of computing. The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, shared with John Hopfield, recognised the foundations of machine learning with artificial neural networks.

achievements.title: Public warnings on AI risk (2023 onward)
achievements.impact: After leaving Google he became one of the best known scientists warning about AI, from misinformation and job losses to the chance that advanced systems escape human control. He has also rejected the idea that the industry can regulate itself.
